A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new approach to group key distribution, called self-healing, that allows a user to recover lost group keys on his/her own, without the need for the group manager to transmit the lost keys.

self-healing key distribution is a mechanism that allows a group manager to distribute a key to a group of users in such a way that a user who has missed the key distribution can recover the key on its own, without requesting the group manager for the key or requesting additional transmissions.
we provide an efficient, stateless and secure key distribution protocol for dynamic groups, which is also robust against node compromise.

self-healing is an effective way to reduce the number of key transmissions in group key distribution.

the group manager can use self-healing to broadcast a key to all group members without having to send individual retransmissions to users who have missed a broadcast, thus cutting back on both network traffic and the group manager’s workload.
